title: Prefill zero-copy page projection and graceful tenant handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a zero-copy prefill adapter plus a compact page projection layer that exposes non-contiguous underlying KV pages as contiguous logical views to the decoder/kernel selector. The feature enables faster prefill and decode handoff for long-context workloads by avoiding expensive memcpy/refill cycles, reducing prefill latency and peak GPU memory pressure. Additionally implement a graceful tenant handoff protocol that leverages small decode slack windows to move residency without hard-evict spikes, improving tail latency under contention.
background: Current prefill flow copies sparse KV pages into contiguous buffers before decode, which adds 4-12ms per long-prefill for 8k+ contexts and causes extra temporary memory allocations that increase OOM risk on high-util hosts. Existing eviction is abrupt and can spike tail latency for other tenants during aggressive compaction. We need a runtime-level projection that (1) maps page fragments into a read-only GPU addressable view and (2) schedules cooperative handoffs using decode slack and temporary replicated bloom hints so decodes can proceed without hard waits.
goals: Reduce median prefill latency for 8k context prompts by >=25%
Lower peak temporary allocation during prefill by >=40%
Eliminate hard-evict stalls for crossing-tenant compaction events (measured by p99 latency regressions)
Keep compatibility with quantized kernels and streaming responses
non_goals: End-to-end zero-copy for every kernel path (initial rollout covers favored kernels)
Replacing global eviction policy entirely (we add a cooperative handoff path)
solution_summary: Implement a 'page projection' abstraction: a lightweight descriptor table that lets kernels access fragmented KV slices through a scatter-gather mapping exposed as a contiguous logical base pointer. Add a zero-copy prefill adapter that populates descriptors (no memcpy) and a short-lived read-only residency view used by the decoder. For eviction, implement a tenant handoff protocol: when eviction needed, runtime marks pages with a 'handoff intent' flag, brokers a small decode slack window (e.g., 1-3 tokens) and either migrates hot fragments to a transient read-replicas buffer or defers eviction until the slack completes. Metrics and heuristics guide whether to migrate or defer.
design_tradeoffs: Complexity vs benefit: descriptor table and scatter-gather adds indirection; benefits are lower latency and memory churn but complicates kernel pointer arithmetic
Security/isolation: zero-copy increases importance of strict read-only enforcement and KMS-backed page encryption for Private deployments; requires additional memory protection checks
Compatibility: favor supported kernels first (fast-attn-v2, tiled-matmul) and fall back to memcpy path for older kernels
Resource overhead: transient read-replica buffer consumes memory; we limit size and use probabilistic selection to avoid runaway replication
implementation_plan: Runtime: add descriptor table, scatter-gather ABI, and page projection helpers
Kernel adapters: modify favored kernels to accept descriptor view; implement fallbacks
Prefill adapter: populate descriptors atomically and publish residency epochs
Eviction/handoff: add handoff intent flag, broker slack window, implement migrate-or-defer heuristic
Safety: enforce read-only GPU mappings and add unit tests for isolation
Rollout: feature flag, canary on dedicated pool, monitor metrics before wider roll
acceptance_criteria: Bench: >25% reduction in median prefill latency for 8k baseline workload (measured vs master)
Bench: peak temporary allocations reduced by >40% during prefill on 3090/RTX-hosts
No regression on function-call structured output or streaming in canary pool
Security review signed off for Private deployments (memory mapping checks)
